And Another vs Union Of India And Others on 8 March, 2024
D/L.30.
March 8, 2024. 
Mns.
 Wpa No. 28958 of 2022 
 + 
 Can 1 of 2023
 M/s. Mokalbari Kanoi Tea Estate Pvt. Ltd. 
 and another
 Vs.
 Union of India and others
 Mr. N. K. Chowdhury,
 Mr. Arijit Chakraborti,
 Mr. Nilotpal Chowdhury,
 Mr. Deepak Sharma
 ... for the petitioners.
 Mr. Mr. K. K. Maiti 
 ...for the respondent no. 4. 
Ms. Manika Roy ...for the Fssai. 
Re: Can 1 of 2023 (modification)
1. The Food Safety and Standard Authority of India (Fssai) has filed the present modification
application for modifying/clarifying the order dated September 5, 2023 passed in Wpa No. 28958
of 2022. 
2. Learned counsel for the applicant points out that in paragraph no. 18 of the order, the court had
directed that the respondent authorities, including the said authority, should also conduct a physical
sample examination of the writ petitioner's' products for the purpose of ascertaining the veracity of
the petitioners' contentions, before coming to a finding as to whether the 'best before' date disclosed
in the labels of the petitioners, that is, June, 2025 is the actual 'best before' date or that printed in
the packages, that is, twelve months from the date of manufacturing. 
3.  It is submitted that the term "physical sample examination" does not find place in the regulations governing the applicant-authority and, as such, there is no provision for the same.
4. Learned counsel points out that the procedure is to have a visual inspection first and thereafter to proceed with drawing of samples and examination thereof. 
5. Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties, it transpires that the issue sought to be raised in the modification application has already been decided conclusively in the writ petition itself.

1 6. In paragraph no. 4 of the order dated September 5, 2023, the Court had observed that the entire premise of the consideration of the respondent authorities was a visual inspection. However,
nothing is depicted in the repeated refusals by the respondent authorities, at the first instance and thereafter on the two review prayers made by the petitioners, to show as to what was the reason for accepting the pre-prints in the packages, which indicated that twelve months was the 'best before'
period, overriding the labels put by the manufacturers themselves. 
7. In the very next paragraph, it was observed that in the absence of any such reason, the petitioners argued that the authorities ought to have physically sampled the products and satisfied themselves by appointing experts as to whether the 'best before' date was yet to come. 
8. In paragraph no. 9 of the order, it was recorded that drawing of sample, it was argued, was subject to satisfactory compliance of necessary provisions of labelling and display, physical condition of the consignment/product and satisfying the balanced shelf-life, failing which the consignment can be rejected at visual inspection stage. Such argument was made on behalf of the respondents. 
9. Upon fully considering the said arguments of both sides, the court came to a reasoned finding that in the present case there was nothing to indicate that there was ever any sampling or physical examination of the consignment or product to verify as to whether the shelf-life indicated in the labels of the petitioners were correct or that which was pre- printed in the packages of the product. 
In the absence of such examination, the refusal by the respondent authorities was held to be vitiated. 
10. Only in such context, in paragraph no. 18 of the judgment, the Court had directed that the respondent-authorities should also conduct a physical sample examination of the petitioners'
products. There is, in any event, no conflict between drawing of sample and physical examination of such sample. 
11. Hence, the issue now sought to be raised by the petitioner was raised at the time of deciding the writ petition and was conclusively determined. Since the order has attained finality, there is no scope of recalling the same, modifying and/or giving any clarification as the order is self-explanatory and need not be clarified further. 
12. Accordingly, 1 of 2023 filed in connection with WPA No. 28958 of 2022 is dismissed. 
13. There will be no order as to costs. 
14. Since the writ petition itself had been disposed earlier, no further order need be passed in that regard. 
15. Urgent photostat certified copies of this order, if applied for, be made available to the parties upon compliance with the requisite formalities.
